terms.title: Move characteristic
terms.summary: The maximum distance, in inches, a model can normally move across the battlefield.

terms.title: Toughness characteristic
terms.summary: A measure of how difficult a model is to wound.

terms.title: Save characteristic
terms.summary: The result required for a successful armour saving throw.

terms.title: Invulnerable Save characteristic
terms.summary: An alternative saving throw that is not modified by Armour Penetration.

terms.title: Wounds characteristic
terms.summary: The amount of damage a model can suffer before it is destroyed.

terms.title: Leadership characteristic
terms.summary: The result used when a model or unit makes a Leadership roll.

terms.title: Range characteristic
terms.summary: The maximum distance at which a weapon can select a target.

terms.title: Attacks characteristic
terms.summary: The number of attacks made with a weapon when it is selected.

terms.title: Ballistic Skill characteristic
terms.summary: The unmodified Hit roll required for an attack made with a ranged weapon to score a hit.

terms.title: Weapon Skill characteristic
terms.summary: The unmodified Hit roll required for an attack made with a melee weapon to score a hit.

terms.title: Strength characteristic
terms.summary: The value compared with the target's Toughness when making a Wound roll.

terms.title: Armour Penetration characteristic
terms.summary: The modifier applied to an armour saving throw made against an attack.

terms.title: Damage characteristic
terms.summary: The number of wounds lost by a model when an allocated attack inflicts damage.

terms.title: Battle Round
terms.summary: A battle round contains one player turn for each player, resolved in the mission's specified order.

terms.title: Player Turn
terms.summary: A player's sequence of start-of-turn, Command, Movement, Shooting, Charge, Fight and end-of-turn steps.

terms.title: Command Phase
terms.summary: The phase in which Command points are gained, Command abilities are resolved and Battle-shock is checked.

terms.title: Movement Phase
terms.summary: The phase in which eligible units make Normal, Advance, Fall Back or Remain Stationary moves and Reinforcements arrive.

terms.title: Shooting Phase
terms.summary: The phase in which eligible units are selected to shoot and resolve ranged attacks.

terms.title: Charge Phase
terms.summary: The phase in which eligible units declare and resolve charges.

terms.title: Fight Phase
terms.summary: The phase in which eligible units pile in, make melee attacks and consolidate.

terms.title: Declare Battle Formations step
terms.summary: The pre-battle step in which players record Leaders, Bodyguard units, embarked units and units starting in Reserves.

terms.title: Reinforcements step
terms.summary: Rules that refer to the Reinforcements step are resolved during the Move Units step; 11E has no separate Reinforcements step.

terms.title: Starting Strength
terms.summary: The number of models in a unit at the start of the first battle round; an Attached unit uses its combined model count.
terms.definition: The number of models a unit contains at the start of the first battle round is its Starting Strength. An Attached unit uses the number of models it contains at that time.

terms.title: Half-strength
terms.summary: A unit is at Half-strength when its remaining models equal half its Starting Strength; a one-model unit instead compares remaining wounds with its W characteristic.
terms.definition: For a unit with Starting Strength 2 or more, it is at Half-strength when its remaining model count equals half its Starting Strength. For Starting Strength 1, its model is at Half-strength when its remaining wounds equal half its W characteristic. If the relevant value cannot be divided evenly, the unit cannot be exactly at Half-strength.

terms.title: Below Starting Strength
terms.summary: A multi-model unit is Below Starting Strength when it has fewer models than its Starting Strength; a one-model unit is below it when remaining wounds are below its W characteristic.

terms.title: Below Half-strength
terms.summary: A multi-model unit is Below Half-strength below half its Starting Strength; a one-model unit is below it when remaining wounds are below half its W characteristic.
terms.definition: For Starting Strength 2 or more, compare remaining models with half the Starting Strength. For Starting Strength 1, compare the model's remaining wounds with half its W characteristic. Odd values cannot be exactly at Half-strength, but can still be Below Half-strength.

terms.title: Destroyed
terms.summary: A destroyed model is removed from the battlefield; a unit is destroyed when its last model is destroyed.

terms.title: Revived
terms.summary: A destroyed model returned to the battlefield by a rule, following that rule's placement restrictions.

terms.title: Objective Marker
terms.summary: A battlefield marker whose control is determined using nearby models' Objective Control characteristics.

terms.title: Deployment Zone
terms.summary: The area of the battlefield in which a mission permits a player to deploy their army.

terms.title: Bodyguard
terms.summary: A unit that an eligible Leader or Support unit can join to form an Attached unit.

terms.title: Action
terms.summary: A mission or rule activity started and completed by an eligible unit under the Actions rules.

terms.title: Detachment
terms.summary: The selected army rules package that provides a Detachment rule and may include Enhancements and Stratagems.

terms.title: Strategic Reserves
terms.summary: Units placed aside before or during battle and later set up using the Strategic Reserves rules.

terms.title: Fire Overwatch
terms.summary: 1CP at the end of the opponent's Movement phase: one friendly unengaged non-TITANIC unit shoots using Snap Shooting.
terms.definition: WHEN: End of your opponent's Movement phase. TARGET: One friendly unengaged unit, excluding TITANIC units. EFFECT: That unit shoots using Snap Shooting.

terms.title: Battle-shocked
terms.summary: A Battle-shocked unit has OC ‘-’, cannot be targeted by its controller's Stratagems, and cannot start or complete Actions.
terms.definition: While a unit is Battle-shocked, every model in it has its OC characteristic modified to ‘-’, its controlling player cannot target it with Stratagems, it cannot start an Action, and any Action it has started cannot be completed.

terms.title: Plague
terms.summary: One of three Death Guard Army Rule effects selected during Declare Battle Formations; the chosen Plague applies to every Afflicted enemy unit.
terms.definition: During Declare Battle Formations, select one Plague from Nurgle’s Gift: Skullsquirm Blight, Rattlejoint Ague or Scabrous Soulrot. Until the end of the battle, every Afflicted enemy unit has the effect of that chosen Plague in addition to the normal Toughness reduction.

terms.title: Damage roll
terms.summary: A roll made to determine a weapon's random Damage characteristic before that damage is inflicted.
terms.definition: When a weapon has a random Damage characteristic, make the indicated roll to determine its Damage value when required by the attack sequence.

terms.title: CHAOS
terms.summary: A faction keyword used by rules that explicitly select CHAOS models or units.
terms.definition: CHAOS identifies models and units for any rule whose target or effect explicitly requires the CHAOS keyword.

terms.title: DAEMON
terms.summary: A keyword used by rules that explicitly select DAEMON models or units.
terms.definition: DAEMON identifies models and units for any rule whose target or effect explicitly requires the DAEMON keyword.

terms.title: GRENADES
terms.summary: An eligible GRENADES unit can be selected for the EXPLOSIVES Core Stratagem.
terms.definition: GRENADES identifies units that can be selected as the target of the EXPLOSIVES Core Stratagem while they meet that Stratagem's other requirements.

terms.title: NURGLE
terms.summary: A faction keyword used by rules that explicitly select NURGLE models or units.
terms.definition: NURGLE identifies models and units for any rule whose target or effect explicitly requires the NURGLE keyword.

terms.title: PSYKER
terms.summary: PSYKER identifies models and units that use or interact with Psychic abilities and weapons.
terms.definition: PSYKER identifies models and units for Psychic abilities, Psychic weapons and any rule whose target or effect explicitly requires a PSYKER.

terms.title: TERMINATOR
terms.summary: TERMINATOR identifies models whose transport capacity and other rules can be handled differently.
terms.definition: TERMINATOR identifies models for Transport Capacity restrictions and any other rule whose target or effect explicitly requires a TERMINATOR.
